what_changed.headline: Energy-led inflation is reaccelerating while core pressures remain comparatively contained.
what_changed.significance: The shock raises near-term policy risk without yet demonstrating broad demand-driven persistence.
what_changed.transmission: Higher energy costs lift headline inflation and expectations; central banks may keep policy restrictive, weighing on duration and rate-sensitive assets.

what_changed.headline: Global long-end yields have risen alongside fiscal and inflation concerns.
what_changed.significance: The move complicates both duration exposure and currency interpretation.
what_changed.transmission: Higher term premia and borrowing costs tighten financial conditions; if driven by fiscal concerns rather than stronger growth, currency support may be weaker.

executive_decisions.development: Treat the energy shock as a supply-side inflation risk, not yet as proof of generalized demand overheating.
executive_decisions.why_it_matters: The ECB identifies energy supply shocks as the dominant driver, while euro-area core inflation has remained contained; policy response may therefore be gradual but restrictive.
executive_decisions.transmission: Further energy escalation can delay easing and pressure duration, consumption and inflation-sensitive currencies.

executive_decisions.development: Keep duration exposure selective while monitoring whether long-end yield pressure persists.
executive_decisions.why_it_matters: US, German and Japanese benchmark yields have reached multi-year highs, with sources citing inflation, issuance and debt-sustainability concerns.
executive_decisions.transmission: Persistent term-premium pressure can tighten global financial conditions even without additional policy-rate increases.

regime_dashboard.state: Energy and food pressures are elevated; core inflation is mixed across regions.
regime_dashboard.confidence_rationale: Code-calibrated evidence strength: 2 cited document(s) from 2 conservatively independent evidence family/families from 2 publisher(s); strongest tier is primary. Explicit counterevidence reduces the displayed tier.

evidence.text: Euro-area headline inflation rose to 3.3% in August, while core inflation fell to 2.4%.
The ECB estimates that the January-May 2026 increase was driven almost entirely by adverse energy supply shocks.

counterevidence.text: Euro-area services inflation fell to 3.0% and no significant energy pass-through to core inflation had materialised by August.

regime_dashboard.state: Restrictive bias remains, with hike risk where inflation is above target.
regime_dashboard.confidence_rationale: Code-calibrated evidence strength: 4 cited document(s) from 1 conservatively independent evidence family/families from 3 publisher(s); strongest tier is primary. Explicit counterevidence reduces the displayed tier.

evidence.text: Norges Bank kept its policy rate at 4.25% and said a further increase may still be necessary.
The Reserve Bank of Australia judged monetary policy to be somewhat restrictive.
A Federal Reserve governor said rates should rise decisively if inflation does not moderate sufficiently.

counterevidence.text: The ECB describes its response to the predominantly supply-side shock as gradual and flexible.

regime_dashboard.confidence_rationale: Code-calibrated evidence strength: 3 cited document(s) from 1 conservatively independent evidence family/families from 1 publisher(s); strongest tier is institutional_analysis. At least one cited document has an acquisition-quality warning. Explicit counterevidence reduces the displayed tier.

evidence.text: US manufacturing remained in expansion at an ISM reading of 54.6 in August, while employment moderated.
Italian GDP grew 0.2% quarter-on-quarter in Q2, supported by domestic demand.

counterevidence.text: Hungarian investment fell 3.6% quarter-on-quarter in Q2 and the capital stock has stagnated for almost four years.

regime_dashboard.confidence_rationale: Code-calibrated evidence strength: 2 cited document(s) from 1 conservatively independent evidence family/families from 1 publisher(s); strongest tier is market_interpretation.

evidence.text: The US 10-year yield traded above 4.75%, while German and Japanese 10-year yields reached multi-year highs.
The yield rise was attributed to policy expectations, inflation uncertainty, sovereign issuance and fiscal risks.

regime_dashboard.confidence_rationale: Code-calibrated evidence strength: 2 cited document(s) from 2 conservatively independent evidence family/families from 2 publisher(s); strongest tier is primary.

evidence.text: Saxo reported that higher oil prices and rising global bond yields weighed on stocks.
Geopolitical risk has significantly worsened euro-area household sentiment and spending intentions, according to cited ECB research.

regime_dashboard.confidence_rationale: Code-calibrated evidence strength: 2 cited document(s) from 1 conservatively independent evidence family/families from 2 publisher(s); strongest tier is institutional_analysis. Explicit counterevidence reduces the displayed tier.

evidence.text: ING estimates the proposed Czech 2027 deficit at 3.5% of GDP after municipal adjustment.
J.P. Morgan analysts expect higher national oil transfers and a larger fiscal impulse in Kazakhstan next year.

counterevidence.text: Fiscal consolidation was identified as part of Turkey’s disinflation programme.

macro_themes.thesis: Energy and food disruptions are lifting headline inflation while demand-side pressures remain uneven, forcing central banks to balance credibility against growth.
macro_themes.market_implication: Near-term duration risk is asymmetric if energy escalation persists; the strongest pressure is likely on energy-importing economies and rate-sensitive demand.

observed_facts.text: Euro-area headline inflation rose to 3.3% in August, driven by energy, while core inflation fell to 2.4%.
Turkey reported July consumer inflation of 31.8% and maintained a tight stance amid geopolitical supply shocks.

inferences.text: If energy disruptions persist, policy easing may be delayed even where core inflation and demand are relatively benign.

conflicting_evidence.text: ECB analysis supports a measured response to the supply shock, while Norges Bank and some US commentary retain explicit tightening risk.

unresolved_questions: Will energy costs pass through into core inflation and wages?
Will fiscal support offset or amplify the supply shock?

transmission.implication: Bearish for duration if energy inflation persists and central banks delay easing.
Potential support for currencies of central banks retaining a tightening bias; energy importers remain vulnerable.
Constructive for energy and agriculture while supply disruptions persist.
Margin and valuation pressure for energy-intensive and rate-sensitive sectors.

catalysts: Further developments around Middle East energy flows
invalidation_conditions: Energy prices stabilise and core inflation continues to decline
Demand weakens enough to force a clear shift toward easing

macro_themes.theme: AI investment is broadening, but labour and productivity effects remain uncertain
macro_themes.thesis: AI adoption is widespread and supporting investment, yet current evidence points more to workflow transformation and retraining than large-scale displacement.
macro_themes.market_implication: The durable opportunity may extend beyond software and semiconductors into power, grids, infrastructure and productivity-enhancing capital.

observed_facts.text: More than 60% of surveyed service firms and about half of manufacturers reported using AI; layoffs remained uncommon.
A Federal Reserve governor said US growth was powered in part by AI-related business investment and capability buildout.

inferences.text: AI-related capital expenditure can support near-term activity without yet producing a broad employment shock; power and grid constraints may become important transmission channels.

conflicting_evidence.text: New York Fed survey evidence finds limited layoffs, while cited research warns that entry-level workers may face greater substitution risk.

unresolved_questions: Will productivity gains broaden beyond leading firms and sectors?
Will AI investment remain resilient under higher financing costs?

transmission.implication: Supports AI, semiconductor and enabling-infrastructure investment, but with valuation and execution risk.
Supports electricity, industrial metals and grid-related demand over the medium term.
Could support growth, but associated capex and power demand may complicate inflation assessment.

catalysts: Corporate AI investment and adoption data
invalidation_conditions: AI capex materially weakens or adoption fails to improve productivity
Higher financing costs cause widespread project cancellations

asset_views.thesis: Persistent energy inflation and fiscal/term-premium concerns can delay easing and keep long-end yields elevated.
asset_views.transmission: Higher inflation compensation and issuance concerns raise discount rates and tighten financial conditions.
drivers: US inflation remains above target according to Federal Reserve commentary.
Energy prices remain a renewed inflation risk.
risks: Weak payrolls or services data could reduce tightening expectations.
Treasury intervention or fiscal measures could lower long-end yields.
asset_views.catalyst: US labour, services and inflation data.
asset_views.invalidation_condition: A sustained sequence of softer inflation and activity data leads to clear easing guidance.

evidence.text: A Federal Reserve governor said rates should rise decisively if inflation does not moderate sufficiently.

counterevidence.text: ING expects limited wage pressure and says a possible September hike would not require a series of hikes.

asset_views.confidence_rationale: Code-calibrated evidence strength: 2 cited document(s) from 2 conservatively independent evidence family/families from 2 publisher(s); strongest tier is primary. Explicit counterevidence reduces the displayed tier.
asset_views.thesis: Energy inflation makes near-term easing less likely, while core containment limits the case for sustained restrictive repricing.
asset_views.transmission: Higher energy costs lift inflation expectations and sovereign yields; weaker real income can later restrain growth.
drivers: ECB analysis characterises the shock as predominantly supply-driven.
risks: Core inflation may remain contained and policy may stay gradual.
A resolution of geopolitical disruptions could lower energy prices.
asset_views.catalyst: Euro-area inflation and ECB policy communication.
asset_views.invalidation_condition: Core inflation and wage growth continue to fall while energy prices normalise.

evidence.text: Euro-area headline inflation rose to 3.3% and energy inflation to 14.3%, while core inflation fell to 2.4%.
The ECB says the 2026 inflation increase has so far been driven almost entirely by energy supply shocks.

counterevidence.text: Euro-area services inflation fell to 3.0% and significant pass-through to core inflation has not yet materialised.

asset_views.confidence_rationale: Code-calibrated evidence strength: 3 cited document(s) from 1 conservatively independent evidence family/families from 1 publisher(s); strongest tier is market_interpretation. Explicit counterevidence reduces the displayed tier.
asset_views.thesis: Geopolitical disruption and agricultural supply risks are sustaining scarcity premia despite tighter financial conditions.
asset_views.transmission: Higher energy and food input costs support commodity prices but pressure consumers, margins and central-bank policy.
drivers: Renewed Middle East conflict is disrupting energy flows.
European gas and refined-product costs remain elevated.
Agriculture has been supported by weather and Black Sea supply risks.
risks: Ceasefire or restored shipping could release risk premia.
Higher rates and weaker growth could reduce demand.
asset_views.invalidation_condition: Energy flows normalise and agricultural supply concerns ease materially.

evidence.text: Crude rose amid renewed hostilities and concerns about disruption through the Strait of Hormuz.
Agriculture reached a 14-year high at the end of August after a 12.4% monthly rise.

counterevidence.text: Saxo identifies Venezuela and other non-OPEC supply as a medium-term counterweight to the oil bullish case.

scenarios.description: Energy-led inflation remains elevated, core inflation rises only gradually, and central banks retain restrictive or cautious guidance.
signposts: Core inflation does not broaden materially.
Policy easing is delayed rather than abandoned.

cross_asset_consequences.implication: Duration remains vulnerable, especially at the long end.
Energy and selected infrastructure outperform rate-sensitive sectors.

assumptions.text: The current euro-area inflation increase remains primarily supply-driven.
AI investment continues to support activity without broad layoffs.

scenarios.description: Energy disruptions ease, inflation expectations stabilise and resilient activity supports risk assets.

cross_asset_consequences.implication: Long-end yields retrace as inflation risk falls.
Broader risk appetite improves, particularly in rate-sensitive sectors.

assumptions.text: A more favourable ceasefire outcome could lower oil prices and inflation.

scenarios.description: Further energy disruption produces broader pass-through, forcing more tightening while weakening consumption and risk appetite.
signposts: Additional disruption around the Strait of Hormuz.
Worsening household sentiment and spending intentions.

cross_asset_consequences.implication: Front-end and long-end yields rise, with curve behaviour dependent on growth expectations.
Energy-intensive, consumer and duration-sensitive equities underperform.
Energy and food rise, while industrial demand becomes more vulnerable.

assumptions.text: Geopolitical risk can worsen household sentiment and spending intentions.
Higher expected gasoline-price growth is associated with higher inflation expectations and uncertainty.
